alignments.definition: An actor deliberately changes the operating function, user scenario, packaging, rights structure or service role of an underused/idle physical asset so the same underlying asset can produce a materially different useful output or utilization stream.
alignments.boundary: Includes observed/reported functional or operating repurposing of already-existing underused physical space/assets. Excludes ordinary maintenance, pure sale without functional change, greenfield construction, financial refinancing without operating-function change, and policy intent with no actor execution event.
counterexamples: An idle property is auctioned once with no new operating scenario.
A new building is constructed for its intended use rather than repurposed.
An asset is revalued or securitized without changing its operating function.
A policy encourages activation but no actor has executed a transformation.
alignments.alignment_rationale: Each supporting source-native claim describes an executed change in the use/operating scenario of an existing underused asset; their downstream industries differ deliberately. The alignment tests a low-level transformation mechanism rather than treating housing, metro retail, hotel space, urban edge space and energy assets as one industry.

alignments.definition: A customer or workflow experiences avoidable loss of context, delay, repetition, responsibility ambiguity or service failure when an AI-handled interaction should transfer to a human or synchronize state with human service.
alignments.boundary: Includes transfer/synchronization failure between AI and human service. Excludes general model hallucination that does not require handoff, dissatisfaction with a human agent alone, and the mere existence of an AI customer-service standard.
counterexamples: An AI answer is wrong but is immediately corrected without transfer friction.
A human-only call center has a long queue with no AI handoff involved.
A standard is published but no transfer/synchronization problem is reported.
alignments.alignment_rationale: The consumer-complaint report and the national-standard interpretation independently describe human-transfer or synchronization failure. Evidence is still too thin and actor-poor to establish a recurring actor-level pattern, so this remains a candidate alignment.
